panel_description: CNF-native HENI vs Stylianou 2021 published per-food values
separates_from: _smoke_heni_literature_panel.py (which is the implementation regression at +-0.1 min gate)

rows.label: Chicken wing (CNF 629 vs Stylianou §S2.2 WWEIA reference)
rows.rationale: CNF 629: roasted plain wing meat+skin (98 mg Na/100g). Stylianou WWEIA reference: likely restaurant/buffalo wing (579 mg Na/100g). Sodium load differs by 6x.

rows.label: Beef hotdog on bun (CNF 4644 vs Stylianou Fig 4)
rows.rationale: CNF "Fast foods, hot dog, plain" includes bun; lower sodium than typical US fast-food + Stylianou worked example.

rows.label: Frankfurter sandwich (CNF 1185+3985 vs Stylianou Fig 2-4)
rows.citation: Stylianou 2021 Fig 2-4 line 1740 (frankfurter sandwich category median, IQR 31-41)
rows.rationale: Stylianou measures full sandwich; CNF row here is just the frankfurter component (60 g).

rows.label: Vegetable pizza (CNF 5862 vs Stylianou Fig 4)
rows.rationale: CNF row is "meat and vegetable" pizza (not pure vegetable); expect more negative.

rows.label: Sardines in tomato sauce (CNF 3054 vs Stylianou Fig 4 extremum)
rows.rationale: Stylianou's very-high HENI for sardines is driven by omega-3 (EPA+DHA) DRF at -81 uDALY/g. Our CNF 3054 extraction may have lower EPA+DHA than Stylianou's WWEIA reference, and the food-group "vegetables" attribution for tomato sauce is missing.

rows.label: Corned beef (CNF 2791 vs Stylianou Fig 4 -ve extremum)
rows.citation: Stylianou 2021 Fig 4 (corned beef + tomato sauce, -ve extremum)
rows.rationale: Stylianou measures the composite "corned beef + tomato sauce" with very high sodium; CNF 2791 is canned corned beef alone (no added tomato sauce sodium).
